# Dash API

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-dash-dots-reference.mjs from the Dash Dots docs (Dot 1.0.0-beta.5). Don't edit by hand. -->

Every `this.dash` call, its types and the helpers in `@monimesl/dot-runtime`. Source: https://docs2.monime.io/docs/products/dash-dots/reference/dash-api


Everything your dot can ask of the phone and of Dash: alerts, the camera, contacts, the network, storage and more. In a page, call it as `this.dash`. In `dot.ts`, it's `dash`.

For the everyday jobs, start with the [Use Dash features](https://docs2.monime.io/docs/products/dash-dots/developers/dash-apis) guide.

## Groups

| Group | Calls | What they do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [UI](#dash-api) | `dash.ui` | Show an alert, or let the person pick a date or a time with the phone's own pickers. |
| [System](#dash-api) | `dash.system` | Vibrate, use the torch, keep the screen on, copy, share, open the dialer or a web page, wait, and read facts about the phone. |
| [Media](#dash-api) | `dash.media` | Let the person take or choose a photo, choose a file from their phone, or scan a QR code. |
| [Contacts](#dash-api) | `dash.contacts` | Let the person choose a phone number from their contacts. |
| [Account](#dash-api) | `dash.account` | Sign the person in to your dot with their Dash account. |
| [Payments](#dash-api) | `dash.payments` | Take a payment in Dash's own payment sheet, by linked account, card or mobile money, and read it back later. |
| [Network](#dash-api) | `dash.network`, `dash.network.http` | Check whether the phone is online, and send requests, downloads and uploads to your server. |
| [Files](#dash-api) | `dash.storage.file` | Keep files on the phone that only your dot can read, and work with the files Dash gives your dot. |
| [Cache](#dash-api) | `dash.storage.cache` | Keep values on the phone for a while, each with an optional expiry time. |
| [Secrets](#dash-api) | `dash.storage.secret` | Keep small private values, such as a session token, encrypted on the phone. |
| [Crypto](#dash-api) | `dash.crypto` | Work out hashes and HMAC signatures, and make random bytes and UUIDs. |
| [Utils](#dash-api) | `dash.utils` | Convert text to base64 or hex and back, without waiting for Dash. |
| [Dot](#dash-api) | `dash.dot` | Close the dot from your code, the same as going back from its first page. |
| [Helpers](#dash-api) | `@monimesl/dot-runtime` | Tell errors apart, handle a picker the person closed, and search as the person types. |
| [Versions](#dash-api) | `dash` | Check whether the person's Dash has a call, and how Dash API versions work. |

## Calls

Every call returns a `DashRequest`: a promise you await for the result, which you can also cancel. Every call also takes an optional last argument, `CallOptions`, with a `timeout` in milliseconds. Without one, a call waits as long as it takes.

```ts
const request = this.dash.network.http.request({ url: `${env.API_URL}/shows` }, { timeout: 10_000 });
// Later, if the answer is no longer needed:
request.cancel(); // the call fails with `cancelled`
```

A call that fails rejects with a `DashError`, whose `code` says why. See [Helpers](#dash-api) for checking it.

| `code` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `unsupported` | The person's Dash can't do this, such as an older Dash or a phone without a camera. Catch it and offer something else. |
| `denied` | Not allowed: the dot didn't declare the permission in `dot.json`, the person said no, or the address isn't in `network.hosts`. |
| `cancelled` | The call stopped before it finished: you cancelled it, the person closed a picker or scanner, or the page that made it closed. |
| `timeout` | The call took longer than the `timeout` you gave it. |
| `invalid` | The call's options are wrong, such as an address that doesn't start with https. |
| `missing` | There's nothing there, such as a file the dot hasn't saved yet. |
| `failed` | Dash tried and couldn't finish, such as when a server doesn't answer. |

## UI

Show an alert, or let the person pick a date or a time with the phone's own pickers.

### `dash.ui.alert`

```ts
dash.ui.alert(options: AlertOptions, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<AlertResult>
```

Shows the phone's own alert. Resolves with the action the person chose.

Types: [`AlertOptions`](#alertoptions), [`AlertResult`](#alertresult)

### `dash.ui.pickDate`

```ts
dash.ui.pickDate(options?: PickDateOptions, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<string>
```

Opens the phone's own calendar. Resolves with the chosen date, such as "2026-10-24", or rejects with `cancelled` if the person closes it.

Types: [`PickDateOptions`](#pickdateoptions)

### `dash.ui.pickTime`

```ts
dash.ui.pickTime(options?: PickTimeOptions, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<string>
```

Opens the phone's own clock. Resolves with the chosen time in 24 hours, such as "19:30", or rejects with `cancelled` if the person closes it.

Types: [`PickTimeOptions`](#picktimeoptions)

### Types

#### `AlertAction`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | What the alert resolves with, as `action`, when the person chooses this action. |
| `label` | `string` |  |
| `role` (optional) | `'default' \| 'cancel' \| 'destructive'` | `cancel` closes the alert, and on Android, Back or a tap outside the alert chooses it too. Without a `cancel` action, the alert stays until the person picks one. `destructive` marks something that can't be undone. |

#### `AlertOptions`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` |  |
| `message` (optional) | `string` | Dash ends it with a line naming the dot, such as "From Plasas Kitchen". |
| `actions` (optional) | [`AlertAction[]`](#alertaction) | Default: one OK button. An empty list fails with `invalid`. |

#### `AlertResult`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | `string` | The `id` of the action the person chose. |

#### `PickDateOptions`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` (optional) | `string` |  |
| `value` (optional) | `string` | The date chosen when the picker opens, such as "2026-10-24". |
| `min` (optional) | `string` | The earliest date the person can pick, such as "2026-10-01". |
| `max` (optional) | `string` | The latest date the person can pick, such as "2026-12-31". |

#### `PickTimeOptions`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` (optional) | `string` |  |
| `value` (optional) | `string` | A time of day in 24 hours, such as "19:30", chosen when the picker opens. |

## System

Vibrate, use the torch, keep the screen on, copy, share, open the dialer or a web page, wait, and read facts about the phone.

### `dash.system.info`

```ts
dash.system.info(callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<SystemInfo>
```

Facts about the phone and Dash: the platform, language, region, time zone and versions. Nothing in it identifies the person or the phone.

Types: [`SystemInfo`](#systeminfo)

### `dash.system.vibrate`

```ts
dash.system.vibrate(options?: VibrateOptions, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<void>
```

Plays a short vibration. Resolves once it's done.

Types: [`VibrateOptions`](#vibrateoptions)

### `dash.system.torch`

```ts
dash.system.torch(on: boolean, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<void>
```

Turns the torch on or off. Rejects with `unsupported` on a device without one.

### `dash.system.keepAwake`

```ts
dash.system.keepAwake(on: boolean, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<void>
```

Keeps the screen from dimming and locking while the dot shows, such as while a ticket's QR code is up. Dash undoes it when the dot closes.

### `dash.system.brightness`

```ts
dash.system.brightness(level: BrightnessLevel, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<void>
```

`max` makes the screen as bright as it goes, so a scanner can read a QR code on it, and `normal` puts it back. Dash puts it back too when the dot closes or the person leaves the app.

Types: [`BrightnessLevel`](#brightnesslevel)

### `dash.system.copyText`

```ts
dash.system.copyText(text: string, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<void>
```

Copies `text` for the person to paste somewhere else.

### `dash.system.share`

```ts
dash.system.share(options: ShareOptions, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<void>
```

Opens the device's share sheet. Resolves once it shows.

Types: [`ShareOptions`](#shareoptions)

### `dash.system.dial`

```ts
dash.system.dial(number: string, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<void>
```

Opens the phone's dialer with `number` ready, such as "+232 76 123456" or a USSD code such as "*715#". The person taps Call. Spaces and dashes are fine; anything else but digits, +, * and # rejects with `invalid`. For a code, Dash asks the person first, and rejects with `cancelled` if they say no. Codes that set up call forwarding, such as "**21*…#", reject with `denied`.

### `dash.system.openUrl`

```ts
dash.system.openUrl(url: string, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<void>
```

Opens an https address in the device's browser. Any other address rejects with `invalid`.

### `dash.system.delay`

```ts
dash.system.delay(milliseconds: number, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<void>
```

Waits `milliseconds`, then resolves. A dot has no `setTimeout`: use this to pause, as between checks on a payment.

### Types

#### `Platform`

```ts
type Platform = 'ios' | 'android' | 'simulator';
```

#### `SystemInfo`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `platform` | [`Platform`](#platform) |  |
| `osVersion` | `string` | Such as "18.2" on iOS or "15" on Android. |
| `language` | `string` | The person's language, such as "en". |
| `region` | `string \| null` | The person's region, such as "SL", or null if Dash doesn't know it. |
| `timeZone` | `string` | Such as "Africa/Freetown". |
| `dashVersion` | `string` | The version of Dash the dot runs in, such as "2.4.0". To check for a call, use `dash.supports`. |
| `apiVersions` | `string[]` | The Dash API versions it offers, one for each major it supports, such as ["1.0"]. |

#### `VibrationStyle`

```ts
type VibrationStyle = 'light' | 'medium' | 'heavy' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error';
```

#### `VibrateOptions`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `style` (optional) | [`VibrationStyle`](#vibrationstyle) | Default: `medium`. |

#### `BrightnessLevel`

```ts
type BrightnessLevel = 'max' | 'normal';
```

#### `ShareOptions`

Give at least one of `text`, `url` and `file`.

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` (optional) | `string` | A subject, for apps that use one, such as email. |
| `text` (optional) | `string` |  |
| `url` (optional) | `string` |  |
| `file` (optional) | [`DotFile`](#dotfile) |  |

## Media

Let the person take or choose a photo, choose a file from their phone, or scan a QR code.

### `dash.media.pickPhoto`

```ts
dash.media.pickPhoto(options: PickPhotoOptions, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<DotFile>
```

Lets the person choose a photo or take one. Resolves with it as a JPEG of at most 2048 pixels on its longest side, without its location or other details. Rejects with `cancelled` if they close the picker, and with `unsupported` on a device without a camera. Save it with `dash.storage.file.save` to keep it after the dot closes.

Permission in [`dot.json`](https://docs2.monime.io/docs/products/dash-dots/reference/dot-json): `camera` to take a photo, or `photoLibrary` to choose one.

Types: [`PickPhotoOptions`](#pickphotooptions), [`DotFile`](#dotfile)

### `dash.media.pickFile`

```ts
dash.media.pickFile(options?: PickFileOptions, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<DotFile>
```

Lets the person choose a file from their phone, of at most 25 MB. Rejects with `cancelled` if they close the picker, and with `invalid` for a larger file. Like a download, it lasts until the dot closes unless you save it with `dash.storage.file.save`.

Permission in [`dot.json`](https://docs2.monime.io/docs/products/dash-dots/reference/dot-json): `files`.

Types: [`PickFileOptions`](#pickfileoptions), [`DotFile`](#dotfile)

### `dash.media.scanCode`

```ts
dash.media.scanCode(callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<ScannedCode>
```

Opens Dash's scanner until it reads a QR code. Rejects with `cancelled` if the person closes it, and with `unsupported` where Dash has no scanner.

Permission in [`dot.json`](https://docs2.monime.io/docs/products/dash-dots/reference/dot-json): `camera`.

Types: [`ScannedCode`](#scannedcode)

### Types

#### `PhotoSource`

```ts
type PhotoSource = 'library' | 'camera';
```

#### `PickPhotoOptions`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | [`PhotoSource`](#photosource) | `library` needs the `photoLibrary` permission, and `camera` the `camera` permission. |

#### `PickFileOptions`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `types` (optional) | `string[]` | Content types the person may choose, such as 'application/pdf' or 'image/*'. Any file without them. |

#### `CodeFormat`

The kind of code that was scanned. Only QR codes for now.

```ts
type CodeFormat = 'qr';
```

#### `ScannedCode`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `string` | What the code holds, as text. |
| `format` | [`CodeFormat`](#codeformat) |  |

## Contacts

Let the person choose a phone number from their contacts.

### `dash.contacts.pickPhone`

```ts
dash.contacts.pickPhone(callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<PickedContact>
```

Shows the phone's contacts for the person to choose one phone number, such as the number to send money to. The dot sees only the chosen contact. Rejects with `cancelled` if the person closes it.

Permission in [`dot.json`](https://docs2.monime.io/docs/products/dash-dots/reference/dot-json): `contacts`.

Types: [`PickedContact`](#pickedcontact)

### Types

#### `PickedContact`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `phone` | `string` | As the contact has it, such as "+232 76 123456" or "076 123456". |

## Account

Sign the person in to your dot with their Dash account.

### `dash.account.signIn`

```ts
dash.account.signIn(options: SimpleSignInOptions, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<SimpleSignIn>
```

Signs the person in with their Dash account, and gives their full name, their phone number (or email if they have no phone) and an ID for them in your dot. Fails with `denied` if they say no, `failed` if no one is signed in or Dash can't reach Monime, and `invalid` for a nonce over 128 characters.

> **The ID isn't proof.** Your dot sends `accountIdToken` to your server itself, so your server can't tell it from one someone made up. Use it to recognise the person, not to let them into their account or their money on your server.

Permission in [`dot.json`](https://docs2.monime.io/docs/products/dash-dots/reference/dot-json): `account`.

Types: [`SimpleSignInOptions`](#simplesigninoptions), [`SimpleSignIn`](#simplesignin)

### Types

#### `SimpleSignInOptions`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | `'simple'` | Always `'simple'`. |
| `nonce` (optional) | `string` | Leave it out to get the same ID for the person every time. A different nonce gives a different ID, which can't be matched to their others. Up to 128 characters. |

#### `SimpleSignIn`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fullName` | `string` | The person's full name on their Dash account, such as "Aminata Kamara". |
| `alias` | `string` | The phone number or email address the person uses Dash with, such as "+232 76 123456". It's the phone number when the account has one. |
| `accountIdToken` | `string` | An ID for this person in your dot. It's the same on any phone, and different in every other dot. Your server can't verify it came from Dash, so don't treat it as proof. |

## Payments

Take a payment in Dash's own payment sheet, by linked account, card or mobile money, and read it back later.

### `dash.payments.request`

```ts
dash.payments.request(options: PaymentOptions, callOptions?: PaymentCallOptions): DashRequest<PaymentResult>
```

Opens Dash's payment sheet, where the person pays for `order` with one of `methods`. The money goes to the Space that owns the dot.

Before the person picks a method, it can reject with:

- `invalid`: Monime won't take the order, such as one below its smallest amount.
- `denied`: the dot or its Space can't take payments now.
- `failed`: Dash couldn't reach Monime.
- `cancelled`: the person closed the sheet.
- `timeout`: the sheet waited as long as Dash allows.

Once they pick a method, it resolves with the payment's `status`: `completed`, `pending`, `expired`, or `cancelled` if they closed the sheet. If a method fails, the sheet stays open for them to try again. From then on, `cancel()` only stops your code waiting; the payment goes on. Read it again later with `get`.

Permission in [`dot.json`](https://docs2.monime.io/docs/products/dash-dots/reference/dot-json): `payments`.

Types: [`PaymentOptions`](#paymentoptions), [`PaymentCallOptions`](#paymentcalloptions), [`PaymentResult`](#paymentresult)

### `dash.payments.get`

```ts
dash.payments.get(reference: string, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<PaymentResult | undefined>
```

The payment for the order with this reference, to check a pending one later or after the dot opens again. Undefined if this dot never asked for it, or the person never picked a method.

Permission in [`dot.json`](https://docs2.monime.io/docs/products/dash-dots/reference/dot-json): `payments`.

Types: [`PaymentResult`](#paymentresult)

### Types

#### `Money`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `currency` | `'SLE' \| 'USD'` |  |
| `value` | `number` | In minor units, as in Monime's API: SLE 75.00 is 7500. |

#### `OrderLineItem`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `unitPrice` | [`Money`](#money) |  |
| `quantity` (optional) | `number` | 1 to 100,000. Default: 1. |
| `imageUrl` (optional) | `string` | An https picture Dash shows beside the item. Its host must be in `network.hosts` in `dot.json`. |

#### `Order`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | What the person is paying for, such as "Jazz Night tickets". 3 to 64 characters. |
| `reference` | `string` | The dot's own ID for the order, up to 64 characters. The same reference never pays twice: asking again gives back the first payment. |
| `description` (optional) | `string` |  |
| `lineItems` | [`OrderLineItem[]`](#orderlineitem) | 1 to 16 items, all in one currency. Dash adds them up for the total. |
| `metadata` (optional) | `Record<string, string>` | Up to 64 pairs, with keys up to 48 characters and values up to 100. They stay with the payment and its webhooks. Keys can't start with "@", "_" or "monime", which Monime keeps for itself. |

#### `MomoProvider`

Monime's IDs for the mobile money providers: m17 is Orange Money and m18 is Africell Money.

```ts
type MomoProvider = 'm17' | 'm18';
```

#### `LinkProvider`

Monime's IDs for the banks a linked account can be at.

```ts
type LinkProvider = 'slb001' | 'slb004' | 'slb007' | 'slb009' | 'slb013';
```

#### `LinkMethod`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `'link'` |  |
| `providers` (optional) | [`LinkProvider[]`](#linkprovider) | The only banks that can pay. Empty or left out means any. |

#### `CardMethod`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `'card'` |  |

#### `MomoMethod`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `'momo'` |  |
| `providers` (optional) | [`MomoProvider[]`](#momoprovider) | The only providers that can pay. Empty or left out means both. |
| `phoneNumber` (optional) | `string` | Only this number can pay, such as "+23276123456". |

#### `PaymentMethod`

```ts
type PaymentMethod = LinkMethod | CardMethod | MomoMethod;
```

Types: [`LinkMethod`](#linkmethod), [`CardMethod`](#cardmethod), [`MomoMethod`](#momomethod)

#### `PaymentOptions`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `order` | [`Order`](#order) |  |
| `methods` (optional) | [`PaymentMethod[]`](#paymentmethod) | The methods to offer, in order, each with its own settings. Leave it out for all three with no limits. |
| `financialAccountId` (optional) | `string` | The financial account the money goes to, such as "fac-k6VgVTfSmLruHpiQgMg4DUeySZx". It must belong to the Space that owns the dot and hold the order's currency. Leave it out for the Space's main account. |

#### `PaymentStatus`

`failed` comes only from `get`, for a pending payment that failed later.

```ts
type PaymentStatus = 'pending' | 'completed' | 'failed' | 'expired' | 'cancelled';
```

#### `CardPaymentResult`

Also has the fields of [`PaymentResultBase`](#paymentresultbase).

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `method` | `'card'` |  |
| `checkoutSessionId` | `string` | The Monime checkout session the card paid through. |

#### `MomoPaymentResult`

Also has the fields of [`PaymentResultBase`](#paymentresultbase).

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `method` | `'momo'` |  |
| `paymentCodeId` | `string` | The Monime payment code the mobile money paid through. |

#### `LinkPaymentResult`

Also has the fields of [`PaymentResultBase`](#paymentresultbase).

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `method` | `'link'` |  |
| `paymentId` | `string` | The Monime payment the linked account made. |

#### `PaymentResult`

```ts
type PaymentResult = CardPaymentResult | MomoPaymentResult | LinkPaymentResult;
```

Types: [`CardPaymentResult`](#cardpaymentresult), [`MomoPaymentResult`](#momopaymentresult), [`LinkPaymentResult`](#linkpaymentresult)

#### `PaymentCallOptions`

No `timeout`: Dash decides how long the sheet waits.

```ts
type PaymentCallOptions = Omit<CallOptions, 'timeout'>;
```

Types: [`CallOptions`](#calls)

#### `PaymentResultBase`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reference` | `string` | The order's `reference`. |
| `requestId` | `string` | Dash's ID for the payment request. Give it to Monime's support when asking about a payment. |
| `status` | [`PaymentStatus`](#paymentstatus) | How the payment stands now. |
| `amount` | [`Money`](#money) | The order's total. |
| `paymentId` (optional) | `string` | Monime's payment, such as "pay-…", once there is one. |
| `orderNumber` (optional) | `string` | Monime's number for the order, for the person's receipt and for support. Only once the payment has completed. |

## Network

Check whether the phone is online, and send requests, downloads and uploads to your server.

### `dash.network.status`

```ts
dash.network.status(callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<NetworkStatus>
```

Whether the phone is online now, and how. It can still be online without reaching a server.

Types: [`NetworkStatus`](#networkstatus)

### `dash.network.http.request`

```ts
dash.network.http.request<ResponseBody = string, RequestBody extends HttpRequestBody = HttpRequestBody>(options: HttpRequest<RequestBody> & HttpReadOptions<ResponseBody>, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<HttpResponse<ResponseBody>>
```

Like fetch, resolves with any response, even a 404. An object body is sent as JSON.

Types: [`HttpRequestBody`](#httprequestbody), [`HttpRequest`](#httprequest), [`HttpReadOptions`](#httpreadoptions), [`HttpResponse`](#httpresponse)

### `dash.network.http.download`

```ts
dash.network.http.download(options: HttpDownloadRequest, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<HttpDownloadResponse>
```

Saves a 2xx response's body, up to 256 MB, to a temporary file.

Types: [`HttpDownloadRequest`](#httpdownloadrequest), [`HttpDownloadResponse`](#httpdownloadresponse)

### `dash.network.http.upload`

```ts
dash.network.http.upload<ResponseBody = string>(options: HttpUploadRequest & HttpReadOptions<ResponseBody>, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<HttpResponse<ResponseBody>>
```

Sends files to your server as a multipart form, with any `fields` you add. Pass each file as the `DotFile` you got, such as from `pickPhoto`.

Types: [`HttpUploadRequest`](#httpuploadrequest), [`HttpReadOptions`](#httpreadoptions), [`HttpResponse`](#httpresponse)

### Types

#### `ConnectionType`

```ts
type ConnectionType = 'wifi' | 'cellular' | 'other' | 'none';
```

#### `NetworkStatus`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `online` | `boolean` |  |
| `type` | [`ConnectionType`](#connectiontype) |  |

#### `HttpMethod`

```ts
type HttpMethod = 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'PATCH' | 'DELETE' | 'HEAD' | 'OPTIONS';
```

#### `HttpRequestBody`

```ts
type HttpRequestBody = string | object;
```

#### `HttpRequest`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | `string` | An https address on a host in `network.hosts` in `dot.json`. |
| `method` (optional) | [`HttpMethod`](#httpmethod) | Default: `GET`. |
| `headers` (optional) | `Record<string, string>` |  |
| `body` (optional) | `RequestBody` | Text, or an object, which is sent as JSON. |

#### `HttpResponse`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ok` | `boolean` | True for a status from 200 to 299. |
| `status` | `number` |  |
| `statusText` | `string` |  |
| `headers` | `Record<string, string>` | Names are lowercase, such as "content-type". A header sent more than once comes once, with its values joined by ", ". |
| `body` | `ResponseBody` | Text, or the parsed JSON when you asked for `as: 'json'`. |

#### `HttpReadOptions`

Without `as`, the response body is text. Pass `as: 'json'` to get it parsed, typed as the call's `ResponseBody`.

```ts
type HttpReadOptions<ResponseBody> = [ResponseBody] extends [string]
  ? { as?: 'text' }
  : { as: 'json' };
```

#### `HttpDownloadRequest`

Also has the fields of [`HttpRequest`](#httprequest).

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (optional) | `string` | The file's name. Without it, the name comes from the response or the address. |

#### `HttpDownloadResponse`

```ts
type HttpDownloadResponse =
  | (Omit<HttpResponse, 'ok' | 'body'> & { ok: true; file: DotFile })
  | (Omit<HttpResponse, 'ok'> & { ok: false });
```

Types: [`HttpResponse`](#httpresponse), [`DotFile`](#dotfile)

#### `HttpUploadFile`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `field` | `string` | The form field the file goes in. |
| `file` | [`DotFile`](#dotfile) |  |
| `name` (optional) | `string` | The file name your server sees. Without it, it's the file's own name. |

#### `HttpUploadRequest`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | `string` | An https address on a host in `network.hosts` in `dot.json`. |
| `method` (optional) | `'POST' \| 'PUT' \| 'PATCH'` | Default: `POST`. |
| `headers` (optional) | `Record<string, string>` |  |
| `fields` (optional) | `Record<string, string>` | Text fields sent along with the files. |
| `files` | [`HttpUploadFile[]`](#httpuploadfile) |  |

## Files

Keep files on the phone that only your dot can read, and work with the files Dash gives your dot.

A dot's own data, kept on this device for the signed-in Dash user only. It's never backed up or moved to a new phone, and another user who signs in sees none of it. Keep what matters on the dot's server, and treat this as a copy you can fetch again.

Files live in the dot's own folder, which no other dot sees. Paths are relative to it, such as "receipts/42.pdf", and '' is the folder itself. A call on a path with nothing there fails with `missing`, while `stat` gives null for it.

### `dash.storage.file.read`

```ts
dash.storage.file.read(path: string, options?: ReadOptions, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<string>
```

Reads the file at `path`, up to 5 MB, as text or base64. Fails with `missing` if there's no file there.

Types: [`ReadOptions`](#readoptions)

### `dash.storage.file.write`

```ts
dash.storage.file.write(path: string, data: string, options?: WriteOptions, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<FileEntry>
```

Writes `data` to the file at `path`, as text or base64, and creates any missing folders above it. Pass `{ append: true }` to add to the end of the file.

Types: [`WriteOptions`](#writeoptions), [`FileEntry`](#fileentry)

### `dash.storage.file.stat`

```ts
dash.storage.file.stat(path: string, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<FileEntry | null>
```

Details of the file or folder at `path`: its kind, size and when it last changed. Gives null if there's nothing there.

Types: [`FileEntry`](#fileentry)

### `dash.storage.file.list`

```ts
dash.storage.file.list(path?: string, options?: { recursive?: boolean }, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<FileEntry[]>
```

What a folder holds, sorted by path. Pass `{ recursive: true }` to include everything in its subfolders.

Types: [`FileEntry`](#fileentry)

### `dash.storage.file.createFolder`

```ts
dash.storage.file.createFolder(path: string, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<FileEntry>
```

Creates a folder at `path`, with any folders above it that are missing.

Types: [`FileEntry`](#fileentry)

### `dash.storage.file.move`

```ts
dash.storage.file.move(from: string, to: string, options?: ReplaceOptions, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<FileEntry>
```

Moves or renames a file or folder. Pass `{ overwrite: true }` to replace what's already at `to`.

Types: [`ReplaceOptions`](#replaceoptions), [`FileEntry`](#fileentry)

### `dash.storage.file.copy`

```ts
dash.storage.file.copy(from: string, to: string, options?: ReplaceOptions, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<FileEntry>
```

Copies a file or folder. Pass `{ overwrite: true }` to replace what's already at `to`.

Types: [`ReplaceOptions`](#replaceoptions), [`FileEntry`](#fileentry)

### `dash.storage.file.remove`

```ts
dash.storage.file.remove(path: string, options?: { recursive?: boolean }, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<void>
```

Deletes the file or folder at `path`. A folder with anything in it needs `{ recursive: true }`.

### `dash.storage.file.save`

```ts
dash.storage.file.save(file: DotFile, path: string, options?: ReplaceOptions, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<FileEntry>
```

Keeps a temporary file, such as a download, at `path`.

Types: [`DotFile`](#dotfile), [`ReplaceOptions`](#replaceoptions), [`FileEntry`](#fileentry)

### `dash.storage.file.open`

```ts
dash.storage.file.open(path: string, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<DotFile>
```

A stored file as a DotFile, to show with its `url` or send with `http.upload`.

Types: [`DotFile`](#dotfile)

### `dash.storage.file.usage`

```ts
dash.storage.file.usage(callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<StorageUsage>
```

How many bytes the dot's files take, and the most they may take.

Types: [`StorageUsage`](#storageusage)

### Types

#### `FileEntry`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `path` | `string` |  |
| `size` | `number` | In bytes, and 0 for a folder. |
| `kind` | `'file' \| 'folder'` |  |
| `modifiedAt` | `number` | When it last changed, in milliseconds since 1 January 1970, as Date.now() gives. |
| `contentType` (optional) | `string` |  |

#### `FileEncoding`

```ts
type FileEncoding = 'text' | 'base64';
```

#### `StorageUsage`

In bytes: what the dot's files take, and the most they may take.

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `used` | `number` |  |
| `quota` | `number` |  |

#### `ReadOptions`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `as` (optional) | [`FileEncoding`](#fileencoding) | Default: `text`. |

#### `WriteOptions`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `as` (optional) | [`FileEncoding`](#fileencoding) | How `data` is written. Default: `text`. |
| `append` (optional) | `boolean` | Adds to the end of the file in place of replacing it. Default: `false`. |

#### `ReplaceOptions`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `overwrite` (optional) | `boolean` | Replaces what's already at the path. Default: `false`. |

#### `DotFile`

A file Dash gives your dot, such as a download or a photo. It lasts until the dot closes, unless you save it with `dash.storage.file.save`.

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | Identifies the file to Dash. Pass the whole `DotFile` to calls, not just its `id`. |
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `size` | `number` | In bytes. |
| `contentType` | `string` |  |
| `url` | `string` | An address to show the file with, such as an `Image`'s `src`. It works until the dot closes. |

## Cache

Keep values on the phone for a while, each with an optional expiry time.

A dot's own key-value cache, apart from its files. It holds up to 64 MB of JSON values, each kept until removed or until its `ttl` runs out.

### `dash.storage.cache.get`

```ts
dash.storage.cache.get<Value extends CacheValue = CacheValue>(key: string, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<Value | null>
```

Resolves with null for a missing or expired key.

Types: [`CacheValue`](#cachevalue)

### `dash.storage.cache.set`

```ts
dash.storage.cache.set(key: string, value: CacheValue, options?: CacheSetOptions, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<void>
```

Saves `value` under `key`. Give `{ ttl }` in milliseconds to have it expire, such as 60 000 for a minute; without it, the value stays until you remove it.

Types: [`CacheValue`](#cachevalue), [`CacheSetOptions`](#cachesetoptions)

### `dash.storage.cache.remove`

```ts
dash.storage.cache.remove(key: string, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<void>
```

Deletes the value saved under `key`.

### `dash.storage.cache.exists`

```ts
dash.storage.cache.exists(key: string, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<boolean>
```

Whether a value is saved under `key` and hasn't expired.

### `dash.storage.cache.keys`

```ts
dash.storage.cache.keys(callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<string[]>
```

Every key with a value that hasn't expired, sorted.

### `dash.storage.cache.clear`

```ts
dash.storage.cache.clear(callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<void>
```

Deletes everything in the dot's cache.

### Types

#### `CacheValue`

```ts
type CacheValue = string | number | boolean | CacheValue[] | { [key: string]: CacheValue };
```

#### `CacheSetOptions`

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ttl` (optional) | `number` | How many milliseconds the entry lasts. Without it, or with 0 or less, it lasts until removed. |

## Secrets

Keep small private values, such as a session token, encrypted on the phone.

A dot's secrets, such as tokens its own API gives the person. Holds up to 32 strings of up to 4 KB each, encrypted with a key that never leaves the device. Don't keep the dot's own API keys here: they would ship in its bundle, which anyone can read.

### `dash.storage.secret.get`

```ts
dash.storage.secret.get(key: string, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<string | null>
```

The secret saved under `key`, or null if there isn't one.

### `dash.storage.secret.set`

```ts
dash.storage.secret.set(key: string, value: string, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<void>
```

Saves `value` under `key`, encrypted on the phone.

### `dash.storage.secret.remove`

```ts
dash.storage.secret.remove(key: string, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<void>
```

Deletes the secret saved under `key`. Deleting one that isn't there is fine.

### `dash.storage.secret.clear`

```ts
dash.storage.secret.clear(callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<void>
```

Deletes all of the dot's secrets.

## Crypto

Work out hashes and HMAC signatures, and make random bytes and UUIDs.

### `dash.crypto.sha256`

```ts
dash.crypto.sha256(data: CryptoInput, options?: CryptoOutputOptions, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<string>
```

The SHA-256 hash of `data`, in hex unless you ask for `{ as: 'base64' }`. Pass text, or `{ base64 }` for binary data such as a file's contents.

Types: [`CryptoInput`](#cryptoinput), [`CryptoOutputOptions`](#cryptooutputoptions)

### `dash.crypto.sha512`

```ts
dash.crypto.sha512(data: CryptoInput, options?: CryptoOutputOptions, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<string>
```

The SHA-512 hash of `data`, in hex unless you ask for `{ as: 'base64' }`. Pass text, or `{ base64 }` for binary data.

Types: [`CryptoInput`](#cryptoinput), [`CryptoOutputOptions`](#cryptooutputoptions)

### `dash.crypto.hmac`

```ts
dash.crypto.hmac(options: HmacOptions, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<string>
```

Signs `data` with `key`, as HMAC-SHA256 or HMAC-SHA512, such as `hmac({ algorithm: 'sha256', key, data })`.

Types: [`HmacOptions`](#hmacoptions)

### `dash.crypto.randomBytes`

```ts
dash.crypto.randomBytes(count: number, options?: CryptoOutputOptions, callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<string>
```

`count` secure random bytes, from 1 to 1024.

Types: [`CryptoOutputOptions`](#cryptooutputoptions)

### `dash.crypto.randomUUID`

```ts
dash.crypto.randomUUID(callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<string>
```

A random version 4 UUID, such as "3f0e5c3a-6d1b-4c8e-9a2f-1b7d4e6a9c05".

### Types

#### `CryptoInput`

Text is read as UTF-8. Binary data, such as a file's contents, comes as base64.

```ts
type CryptoInput = string | { base64: string };
```

#### `CryptoOutputOptions`

Hex by default.

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `as` (optional) | `'hex' \| 'base64'` |  |

#### `HmacAlgorithm`

```ts
type HmacAlgorithm = 'sha256' | 'sha512';
```

#### `HmacOptions`

Also has the fields of [`CryptoOutputOptions`](#cryptooutputoptions).

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `algorithm` | [`HmacAlgorithm`](#hmacalgorithm) |  |
| `key` | [`CryptoInput`](#cryptoinput) |  |
| `data` | [`CryptoInput`](#cryptoinput) |  |

## Utils

Convert text to base64 or hex and back, without waiting for Dash.

Helpers that run in the dot itself, so they need no Dash and answer at once, without `await`.

### `dash.utils.base64`

```ts
dash.utils.base64.encode(text: string): string
dash.utils.base64.decode(encoded: string): string
```

Text to base64 and back, as UTF-8: `dash.utils.base64.encode("Salone")` is `"U2Fsb25l"`. `decode` throws for text that isn't base64.

### `dash.utils.hex`

```ts
dash.utils.hex.encode(text: string): string
dash.utils.hex.decode(encoded: string): string
```

Text to hex and back, as UTF-8: `dash.utils.hex.encode("Salone")` is `"53616c6f6e65"`. `decode` throws for text that isn't hex.

## Dot

Close the dot from your code, the same as going back from its first page.

### `dash.dot.close`

```ts
dash.dot.close(callOptions?: CallOptions): DashRequest<void>
```

Closes the dot, as going back from its first page does. Calls still running are cancelled.

## Helpers

Tell errors apart, handle a picker the person closed, and search as the person types.

Import these from `@monimesl/dot-runtime`. A call that fails rejects with a `DashError`, and its `code` says why.

```ts
import { errorMessage, isDashError, unlessCancelled } from '@monimesl/dot-runtime';

const photo = await unlessCancelled(this.dash.media.pickPhoto({ source: 'camera' }));
if (!photo) return; // The person closed the camera.
```

### `isDashError`

```ts
isDashError<Code extends DashErrorCode>(error: unknown, ...codes: Code[]): error is DashError
```

Whether `error` is a Dash call's error, with one of `codes` when you give any. Inside the check, TypeScript knows its `code`.

### `errorMessage`

```ts
errorMessage(error: unknown): string
```

The message to show for anything a call threw, even if it isn't an Error.

### `unlessCancelled`

```ts
unlessCancelled<Result>(call: PromiseLike<Result>): Promise<Result | undefined>
```

Waits for a call, such as a picker, and gives undefined if the person closed it or it was cancelled. Other errors still throw.

### `latest`

```ts
latest(): <Result>(call: DashRequest<Result>) => DashRequest<Result>
```

Each call given to it cancels the one before, so an older answer can't arrive after a newer one. The cancelled call rejects with `cancelled`, which `unlessCancelled` turns into undefined.

```ts
const search = latest();

// In an action: an older search that answers late gives undefined.
const answer = await unlessCancelled(search(this.dash.network.http.request({ url, as: 'json' })));
```

### `debounce`

```ts
debounce(milliseconds: number): (dash: Dash) => Promise<boolean>
```

Resolves true once `milliseconds` pass without another call, such as a pause in typing, and false when a newer call cut the wait short. Pass it the page's `this.dash`.

```ts
const typingPause = debounce(400);

// In an action that runs on each keystroke: go on only once the person stops typing.
if (!(await typingPause(this.dash))) return;
```

## Versions

Check whether the person's Dash has a call, and how Dash API versions work.

The Dash API has a version, and this reference describes version 1.0. A newer minor version, such as 1.1, only adds: new calls, new options and new fields in results. Nothing in 1.0 is removed or renamed within version 1.

`dash.minApiVersion` in `dot.json` is the oldest version your dot needs, `1.0` unless you set it. Dash opens a dot only when it offers that version or a newer one. When a later version adds a call you want, and you still want older Dash to open your dot, check for the call first. `supports` takes the call's name without `dash.`. Say a later version added `dash.media.scanBarcode`:

```ts
if (this.dash.supports('media.scanBarcode')) {
  // Only a Dash that has the call runs this.
}
```

Every call in this reference is in version 1.0.

### `dash.supports`

```ts
dash.supports(feature: DashFeature): boolean
```

Whether this Dash has `feature`: a call, such as `'contacts.pickPhone'`, or a field added to a call later.
